mechaber.1#main: One who is suspected regarding a forbidden matter may not be relied upon regarding edible matters. It contains 20 seifim: One who is suspected of eating forbidden things — whether he is suspected of a d'oraisa prohibition or a d'rabbanan prohibition — may not be relied upon regarding them; and if one dines with him he may not eat from his food regarding matters he is suspected about: {Rama: And some say even from one who is not suspected but whom they do not recognize as having a presumption of kosher status — it is forbidden to buy wine or other things where there is concern of prohibition from him; however if one dines with him one may eat with him (Beit Yosef in the name of Rambam chapter 1 of Forbidden Foods and chapter 3 law 21):}
mechaber.2#main: If he is not suspected of eating forbidden things but is suspected of selling them — one may dine with him and eat with him; and likewise if he sends to his house it is permitted, for the presumption is that from what he himself eats he sends to him. {Rama: (One who transgresses a sin for appetite is not called suspected) (Beit Yosef in the name of Rashba):}
mechaber.3#main: It is permitted to give from one's own food to one suspected of eating forbidden things so that he may prepare or cook for him, and we are not concerned lest he substitute, since he is not suspected of theft; but if one gives to someone who is concerned about his preparation and he is suspected of eating forbidden things — it is forbidden, lest what he gives become spoiled and he substitute his own. How so? If one gave to his mother-in-law who is suspected regarding the prohibition — it is forbidden, for she is ashamed before her son-in-law and wants her daughter's benefit and therefore substitutes bad for good; and likewise one who gives to an innkeeper who is suspected — sometimes she is ashamed before the guest and substitutes bad for good. {Rama: (Nevertheless it is permitted to deposit with him and that he return the items as deposited):}
mechaber.4#main: One suspected regarding one matter is not suspected regarding other matters; but everything needed for that matter he is also suspected regarding — such as one who was suspected of selling milk in a place of fat and would entice the youths to come buy from him with nuts that he gave them — they penalize him that he may not sell even nuts.
mechaber.5#main: One suspected regarding a severe prohibition is suspected regarding a lighter one than it in penalty, unless the severe one is more stringent in people's eyes such that they are more careful about it than the severe one.
mechaber.6#main: One suspected regarding two matters who repented and left suspicion of both of them, and afterward was suspected regarding one of them — even if it is the lighter of the two — we are concerned lest he returned to his way regarding both and he is suspected regarding both.
mechaber.7#main: One who is notorious for one of the transgressions in the Torah except idolatry and public desecration of Shabbat, or who does not believe in the words of our Sages of blessed memory — is believed regarding other prohibitions; and regarding others' property he is believed even regarding that matter to say it is permitted: {Rama: One who is suspected regarding a matter that does not appear to people as a transgression is not called suspected (Rashba siman 64); however regarding that matter he is not believed. One who practices prohibition in some matter because he holds the law is so, or because of a stringency he adopted — may eat with others who practice leniency regarding it, for they will certainly not feed him what he practices as forbidden (Hagahot Mordechai first chapter of Yevamot and Binyamin Zeev 312 and R' Yerucham end Netiv 3 in the name of Rama):}
mechaber.8#main: One suspected regarding the matter is not believed regarding it even under oath.
mechaber.9#main: A convert from gentiles who returned and apostatized out of fear, and likewise an Israelite who sinned out of fear lest they kill him — is a full Israelite and his slaughter is valid and he does not forbid wine by contact.
mechaber.10#main: An informer — his slaughter is valid and he is believed regarding prohibitions {Rama: (and see above siman 2 that some disqualify an informer's slaughter):}
mechaber.11#main: An apostate in one city who believes in idolatry before gentiles and in another city enters a Jewish home and says he is a Jew — does not make libation wine.
mechaber.12#main: The forced ones who remained in their lands — if they conduct themselves with kosher practice among themselves and cannot escape to a place where they can serve God — we rely on their slaughter and do not forbid wine by their contact.
mechaber.13#main: One who sells his fellow something forbidden to eat — if before he ate it became known, he returns what he bought from him and he returns the money; and if after he ate it became known — what he ate he ate and he returns the money; and if the buyer sold it to a gentile or threw it to dogs he pays him the value of tereifah; and if it was something not forbidden to eat but of rabbinic origin, or if the produce still exists — he returns the produce and takes its value; and if he ate them — what he ate he ate and the seller returns nothing; and all benefit-prohibitions even of rabbinic origin — he returns the money and there is no law of sale at all.
mechaber.14#main: One who sold meat and afterward it became known the animal was not checked properly — its law is like one who sold things forbidden by rabbinic enactment: {Rama: And if he sold him something from an animal whose presumption of kosher status was impaired such that a defect arose in it and they cannot check whether it is kosher and must forbid it out of doubt — even so it is as if it were certainly tereifah and he must return the money (responsum of Ribash):}
mechaber.15#main: One who sells forbidden things — they remove him and excommunicate him and he has no remedy until he goes to a place where he is not recognized and returns a significant lost object or slaughters for himself and produces tereifah for himself in a significant matter such that he certainly repented without subterfuge since he is not sparing of his money.
mechaber.16#main: A butcher whose actions prove he wished to mislead the public to feed them tereifot — such as one who cut away adhesions — they remove him; nevertheless he is exempt from paying the animal's value to the owners.
mechaber.17#main: A butcher from whom tereifah issued — he has no excuse to say he was inadvertent.
mechaber.18#main: A butcher from whom tereifot issued because he is not expert — he has a remedy that he learn and become wise: {Rama: And that which he must go to a place where he is not recognized and repent — that is when he acted intentionally or has a presumption of such; but if we can say it happened in error, it suffices with accepting fellowship rules and repenting according to what the judge sees fit (responsum of Rosh and responsum of Ribash) and see above end of siman 64:}
mechaber.19#main: One who says to one suspected of eating gentile cheese: buy me kosher cheese from the expert — and he went and brought it and says: I bought kosher from the expert — he is not believed; from so-and-so the expert I bought — he is believed. If he brought him a gift in the name of one of the experts — he is believed that he is not suspected to substitute. In what case? When he is not suspected of theft; but if he is suspected of theft — all the more so he is suspected of substitution. {Rama: (And all this does not apply to one suspected of a d'oraisa prohibition) (Beit Yosef):}
mechaber.20#main: One suspected of eating things the public are not accustomed to be lenient regarding — he is also suspected to substitute; and some say one does not deposit with him a d'oraisa forbidden item except with two seals {Rama: (and see above siman 118 seif 8):}
